reviews.title: No confirmation on remove is bad design
reviews.text:
Today I was reviewing one of the people that had joined my teams group, and was adding his son’s name as that’s how I identify the parents and their children. I accidentally hit the removed member, and he was just gone.  No confirmation I really wanted to remove him of any kind. 

As an app developer myself, I can tell you this is absolutely horrible form. You never ever let a user blindly delete something without making sure that that’s absolutely what they want to do and that includes removing them from a group because I can’t go back and add the person back without them going through hoops. This is dumb.

I will gladly modify my review when you fix this obvious giant gaping hole in your process

reviews.title: Not very modern
reviews.text:
Would really like to see the chat function overhauled and brought into the 21st-century. It is very rudimentary and unintuitive. It has many limitations that you just don’t see in today’s chat apps. But this app really hasn’t seen any significant development for years. So I don’t really know that the developers even listen or care.

Here are some examples of what I’m talking about:

You can't like or react to comments.
You can't reply to comments, you can only reply to the original message. You should be able to choose a comment, react to it, or reply to it in an indented thread. TeamReach messaging has such bland and basic functionality.
You have to hit the "# comments" link to reply to a comment, or you end up making a new post, which happens very often because it’s non-intuitive.
Comments are ordered with the most recent at the top. You only see the most recent 2 comments. To see more, you have to know to hit the "# Comments" link, which isn't even clear is a link.

You can react to an original message (not any replies/comments) using 1 of six TeamReach-proprietary emoji - very basic and limited.

Uploaded pictures and files are detached from the messages/threads that they are uploaded to. So when you go to look at pictures and files, it's just a scrollable list, with no context, no way to comment on them, no way to like or otherwise react to them.

There is zero search functionality in TeamReach. Nothing. Nada.

The app automatically signs you up using your full real name
